title: conversational-developer-metering-playbook-2026-12-07
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This playbook defines a developer-focused metering and packaging model for conversational (chat/transactional) workloads. It balances simple self-serve onboarding for developers with precise economics for platform teams and enterprise customers. The goal is to make conversational consumption predictable, enable fidelity experiments, and provide clear migration paths from token-only pricing to turn-aware and feature-aware packages.

Goals

- Create a set of packaging primitives that map to developer mental models (turns, messages, API calls) rather than only tokens.
- Preserve fine-grained billing accuracy for enterprise reconciliation and SLO-backed bundles.
- Allow fidelity experiments (e.g., dynamic response fidelity) without surprise charges.
- Provide a rollout plan and telemetry contract so product, sales, and billing can coordinate migrations.

Scope and audience

This document targets product managers, pricing, billing, SDK/SDKs engineers, platform SRE, and developer advocacy. It covers hosted Redwood API conversational endpoints, but recommendations apply to Dedicated and Private with operational notes.

Key concepts and definitions

- Conversation Turn: a developer-initiated logical interaction containing one or more messages (e.g., user prompt + optional system prompt + single assistant response).
- Meter Unit: primary billing unit for this playbook. For conversational packages we introduce two parallel meter units: "turns" and "tokens".
- Fidelity Adjustment: modifier applied to metering to reflect output quality (e.g., high-fidelity decoding, sampling temperature, external tool calls). Applies only when customers opt into fidelity tiers.
- API Call: REST/SDK invocation. API calls remain visible in telemetry but are not the default billing unit for most packages.

Packaging primitives (recommended)

1) Developer Turn Bundle (self-serve): simple pre-paid bundles targeted at small teams and early-stage devs.

| SKU | Included monthly turns | Included tokens | Overage policy | Target persona | Notes |
|-----|------------------------:|---------------:|---------------|---------------|------|
| dev-turns-1 | 50,000 | 5M | tokens billed at standard per-token rate after tokens exhausted; turns not capped | Indie/PLG dev | Cheapest UX for prototyping. |
| dev-turns-2 | 200,000 | 18M | overage tokens + 10% surcharge on turns if > 120% | SMB product teams | Desktop/web chat pilots |

2) Transactional Meter (meter-by-turn with fidelity bands): for apps where each turn has operational value (e.g., shopping checkout, support resolution).

Metering rule: Each turn is billed as base_turn_unit (1 unit) + fidelity_multiplier (1.0, 1.5, 2.5) depending on fidelity band. Tokens are also recorded for reporting and quota enforcement but not charged if customer chooses turn-only mode.

3) Enterprise SLO Bundles: committed monthly reserved bundles with SLO guarantees (latency, availability) and per-turn unit accounting.

Minimum enterprise commitments: 1M committed turns / month or equivalent committed token volume. SLA credits and burst policies described in Billing and SLA section.

Billing and metering rules (detailed)

- Meter attribution: The platform attributes turns to tenants by route_id and api_key. For multi-tenant Shared endpoints, the tenant context header is required for accurate metering.
- Turn composition: The platform computes tokens for all messages in the turn (system + user + assistant) and records total_request_tokens and total_response_tokens. Tokens are available for post-hoc invoicing reconciliation.
- Fidelity multipliers: Defined at the route level. Default fidelity = 1.0. Customer-configured fidelity bands attach modifiers at request-time (overrides require customer permission).
- Overage behavior: If customers exhaust included turns/tokens, billing follows the selected package: pay-as-you-go per-token or per-turn at published overage rates. Enterprise customers may configure throttling or graceful fidelity degradation instead of immediate overage billing.

SLA, credits, and operational thresholds

- Typical SLA for Enterprise Turn Bundles: 99.95% availability for API, p95 request-to-first-byte latency <= 250ms for text-only conversational responses (for routes with dedicated capacity).
- Error budget: 0.05% monthly downtime for covered routes. Credits calculated as percentage of committed monthly charge: 
  - 99.95 - 99.90% => 10% credit
  - 99.90 - 99.00% => 25% credit
  - <99.00% => 50% credit
- Observability thresholds (alerts): p95 latency > 350ms for > 5 minutes, or error rate > 0.5% in 15-minute window triggers oncall paging.

Telemetry and developer UX contract

Minimum telemetry surfaced in Console and billing APIs for every package:

- Per-route time-series: turns/min, tokens/min, mean response tokens, mean request tokens, p50/p95 latency, error rate.
- Per-customer monthly summary: committed vs used turns, committed vs used tokens, fidelity band distribution, overage charges.
- Sampled per-turn trace (1 per 10k turns) stored for 30 days to analyze quality regressions (redact PII).

Developer-facing UX requirements

- SDKs must expose a sample-metering header and an endpoint to query remaining bundle units: GET /v1/billing/usage?window=30d returns JSON with strings indicating counts. Example included in Appendix.
- Console shows a simple toggle: Meter by: [Tokens | Turns] during onboarding. Default is Tokens for free tier, Turns for dev-turn bundles.

Quality/fidelity experimentation guardrails

We must ensure fidelity experiments do not cause unpredictable bills. Required patterns:

1) Explicit Opt-in: fidelity bands other than default require an explicit opt-in at route or account level.
2) Simulated runs: customers should be able to run fidelity simulations that output an estimated monthly charge with 95% confidence interval based on historical traffic patterns.

Design: fidelity experiment flow

1. Customer creates a fidelity experiment in Console or API, selecting target routes and fidelity band.
2. Redwood runs a 24–72 hour shadow run (no billing changes) and provides projected impact (turns, tokens, projected overage).
3. Customer chooses to apply immediately, schedule rollout, or rollback.

Rollout and migration playbook (90 days)

Phase 0 — Prep (weeks -4 to 0)
- Billing and product finalize SKU names and overage rates.
- SDKs and Console expose the meter toggle and usage API.
- Finance configures invoicing templates and tax handling.
- Customer Success compiles a migration FAQ and template emails.

Phase 1 — Pilot (weeks 0–4)
- Select 10 high-usage developer accounts and 3 enterprise alpha partners.
- Run fidelity shadow experiments and publish findings.
- Iterate rate card for dev bundles.

Phase 2 — Ramp (weeks 5–10)
- Open self-serve SKU for new accounts.
- Offer a migration assistant for existing token-only accounts to opt-in to turns-based bundles with a 90-day free trial of fidelity sim.

Phase 3 — Full Launch (weeks 11–12+)
- Launch marketing collateral, update pricing pages, and notify customers in-product.
- Monitor real-time telemetry and hold weekly syncs across product, SRE, billing, and support for first 8 weeks.

Operational ownership and KPIs

- Product (owner): Aisha Patel — responsible for SKU definitions, rollout coordination, and pricing experiments.
- Billing & Finance: Rahul Desai — invoicing templates, ledger integration, tax handling.
- Platform SRE: Mei Chen — telemetry contract, alerting, and SLA calculations.
- Developer Experience: Carlos Vega — SDK and Console UX for meter toggle and usage APIs.

KPIs to track during rollout

- Adoption rate (percentage of eligible accounts switching to turn bundles) — target 18% within 12 weeks.
- Billing stability: variance in monthly invoices per customer — target <7% volatility after migration.
- Number of fidelity experiments run and % that roll to production — target 25 experiments and 40% promotion rate in first 6 months.

Appendix A — Example SDK usage and sample output

cURL example (metering header):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/conversations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Meter: turns" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"route_id":"chat-conversational-1","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Order status for id 91-881"}]}'

Sample usage API response (stringified counts):

{"committed_turns":"1000000","used_turns":"217453","committed_tokens":"12000000","used_tokens":"4,612,231","fidelity_distribution":"default:92%,high:8%","estimated_next_month_overage":"$210"}

Appendix B — Example rate table (internal)

| SKU | Base price / month | Included turns | Overage turn price | Fidelity high multiplier | Notes |
| dev-turns-1 | $49 | 50k | $0.00065 | 1.5x | intro bundle |
| transaction-100k | $2,500 | 100k | $0.00045 | 2.0x | SLA-eligible |
| enterprise-1m | custom | 1M | custom | configurable | committed, includes SLA credits |
